To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photophysical properties of the interlocked systems are strongly influenced by the presence of the macrocycle and that, as a result, the luminescence properties of the rotaxane are different from those of the component porphyrin.

the photophysical behavior of the interlocked structures 3 and 4(4+), in particular the luminescence properties, is strongly dependent on the nature of the central ion, and that in the case of 3, the presence of a second emitting state, which is not present in the free porphyrin, is observed in toluene.
the photophysics of a [4]rotexane containing a Zn(II) porphyrin and a Cu(I) porphyrins are very similar and that the photophisics of the Cu(I) porphyin is similar to the Cu(I) free base porphyrin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of novel rotaxane systems with the aim of developing molecular devices for applications in the fields of optoelectronics and molecular machines.
the synthesis and characterization of new [4]rotaxes containing porphyrin and perylene chromophores.
the synthesis and the photophysical properties of novel [4]rotaxes containing π-extended Zn and Cu porphyrins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the photophysical properties of 3 are very similar to those of the free Zn porphyrinic wheel 2, whereas the Cu(I) [3]rotaxane shows a dramatic decrease of its emission quantum yield, which is explained by the presence of the Cu(I) center.

the interlocked structure does not influence the photophysical properties in any way, and that all the differences in the photophysical properties of the interlocked systems are due to the presence of the Cu(I) center.

the interlocked structure of 3 and 4(4+), which is characterized by a very small energy gap between the π-π* excited states and the ground state, is responsible for the observed luminescence properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the photophysical properties of 3 and 4(4+), in terms of emission quantum yield and excited state lifetimes, are very sensitive to the electronic interactions between the π-extended porphyin chromophores and the macrocycle, and that these interactions are strongly affected by the presence of the metal in the porphyrin ring.

the luminescence properties of the [4]rotxane 3 are similar to those of the Zn porphyrine 2, but the Cu(I) [2]rotaxane displays a very low emission efficiency, which is not due to a quenching process, but rather to an increase in the energy gap between the excited states and the ground state.

the luminescence properties of the [4]rotxane can be tuned by the choice of the metal and of the solvent, but the interlocked structure itself does not significantly affect the photophysical properties of the porphyrin macrocycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite of the presence of strong electronic interactions between the components of the interlocked structures, the NIR luminescence of the [4]rotaxes is not significantly affected with respect to the corresponding monomeric Zn porphyrins.
the photophysical properties of [4]rotaxes can be tuned by the choice of the macrocycle and of the stopper groups, thus allowing the preparation of systems with specific properties.

, although the presence of an electron-donating unit in the stopper of a [4]rotacane can be used to enhance the photoluminescence of the porphyrin, the presence of a second π-extended chromophore, as in 4, can be used to tune the photophysical properties of the system and to induce a red-shifted emission.
